A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Amortized Bayesian Workflow. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original runtime, posterior-quality, calibration, and MCMC-initialization results across four synthetic and real-world inference problems.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds an empirical study of the OOD diagnostic and its rejection threshold in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both versions use forward-KL-trained normalizing flows and the same diagnostic-guided progression from amortized draws through PSIS to initialized ChEES-HMC. V3's pseudocode, broader training formulation, and small-sample PSIS guidance expand documentation without establishing a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate widened-prior GEV datasets, in-distribution Bernoulli GLM datasets, 8,526 mouse psychometric datasets, and 15,000 IAT participants. The new diagnostic study reuses these task and population settings.

E2.justification: The ChEES-HMC runtime baseline, NUTS reference posteriors, and amortized, PSIS-refined, and random initialization comparisons are retained. Newly discussed software and inference approaches are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V3 Appendix D introduces a diagnostic evaluation using roughly 1,000 test datasets per task and eight rejection levels from 0.01 to 0.5. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; v2's default 95th-percentile cutoff and v3's alpha = 0.05 describe the same rejection rule.

E4.justification: V3 Appendix D and Figure 11 add targeted analyses of Mahalanobis distance versus posterior error and sensitivity to the OOD rejection threshold. Existing calibration and initialization analyses remain, including the NUTS study moved from Appendix D to E.

E5.justification: Both versions report median and IQR across 20 datasets for initialization comparisons, median absolute deviations for parameter recovery, and 95% SBC confidence bands. The new threshold analysis follows the existing median/IQR practice; no changed seed, repeated-run, or significance-testing scheme is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds correlation and threshold-sensitivity results: for example, GEV correlations with W1 and MMTV are 0.47 and 0.64, versus -0.46 and -0.13 for Bernoulli GLM. Table 1 newly separates training and inference times, while retaining acceptance counts, workflow totals, and existing benchmark findings; this does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 generalizes the formal training objective from forward KL to expected strictly proper scoring rules, with forward KL retained for the experiments. No new theorem or proof appears. The Mahalanobis equations moved into the main text already existed in v2 Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal conclusions retain the same claims about diagnostic-guided integration, computational reuse, scalability, and posterior quality. V3's new contribution bullets summarize contributions already asserted in v2.

C2.justification: V3 makes applicability boundaries more explicit, including likelihood evaluation, repeated inference, and moderate effective dimensionality, and explains SBC's possible failure to detect prior-like approximations. It develops the existing OOD limitation with evidence that small distances can accompany poor posteriors and that the diagnostic is uninformative for the retained in-distribution GLM setting.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands procedural documentation through Algorithms 1–7, including PSIS tail selection, resampling, valid distinct initializations, and nested-R computation. It adds training guidance, an explicit repository location, and the four-chain NUTS setting. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and preprocessing disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V3 expands positioning relative to probabilistic programming systems and adds references on scoring rules, diagnostics, training tools, and alternative amortized inference. Papamakarios and Murray (2016) is removed. The central positioning as an integration of existing inference components remains.

P1.justification: V3 extensively develops the training, diagnostic, and discussion exposition and reorganizes the appendices. V2's Appendix B diagnostic material moves into Section 2.2.1 and Appendix A, alongside expanded algorithm explanations, a new training-guidance appendix, and revised terminology throughout.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a different document template with changed typography, margins, author layout, headers, and figure placement. Table 1 gains separate training rows, seven algorithm displays and Figure 11 are added, and explanatory figures are revised. The retained NUTS figure is renumbered and its erroneous ChEES-HMC caption reference is corrected.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reproducibility and assessment through explicit pseudocode, clearer timing breakdowns, and targeted validation of the OOD diagnostic. Its expanded limitations better explain when escalation is needed. These are useful refinements to an already supported workflow; the main empirical evidence remains unchanged and the diagnostic's accuracy limitation persists.
